newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ELCOTEQ ESTONIA MAKES NEW ERICSSON PHONES.
newsitem.headline: ELCOTEQ ESTONIA MAKES NEW ERICSSON PHONES.

text.p: The Estonian factory of Finnish electronics group Elcoteq Network Oy has begun making the new digital GSM mobile phones of Swedish electronics giant Ericsson, Elcoteq said on Tuesday.
During the past year, Elcoteq has tripled the capacity of its Tallinn production facility and the Finnish company is now Estonia's largest exporter.
"We have already started production of Ericsson's new GSM mobile phone in Estonia," Osmo Kammonen, Elcoteq director of corporate communications told Reuters.

In a statement, the Finnish-based company said that Elcoteq expects the deal to have a positive impact on Elcoteq's 1998 performance and with other projects the company expects sales to exceed two billion Finnish marka.
The phones are manufactured in high volumes in a box build mode, which means that Elcoteq delivers finished, quality control tested and packaged products to Ericsson.

"This new project is based on our previous good expereince of Elcoteq's ability to manufacture to our specifications," Jan Ahrenbring, vice president of Ericsson mobile communications, said in the statement.
